Consult Summary:
- 40-year-old woman with 2-day history of wheeze and shortness of breath after dust exposure while cleaning; symptoms worse at night and sometimes limit ability to complete sentences; history of childhood asthma and seasonal hay fever; advised to attend in-person clinic for assessment (including pulse oximetry), consider antihistamine, and possible steroids pending evaluation.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Wheezing and shortness of breath.
- Timeline:
  - Onset: ~2 days ago, starting about an hour after cleaning dusty carpet.
  - Course: Persistent; worse at night; not improving.
- Triggers/relief: Likely triggered by dust exposure. No medications taken yet.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Present: Shortness of breath; sometimes unable to complete sentences when talking.
  - Absent: Chest pain with deep breath; dizziness.
- Intake: Eating/drinking okay; reports 4–5 glasses of water/day.
- Pertinent negatives: No dizziness; no pleuritic pain.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma in childhood; occasional exertional symptoms as an adult; has an inhaler at home; not followed regularly for asthma.
- Seasonal allergic rhinitis (hay fever) in summer; usually untreated.
- Prior use of steroids for asthma (details not provided).

Medications:
- Asthma inhaler at home (type/dose/route/frequency not documented); not used for current episode.
- No other routine medications mentioned.

Allergies:
- No known allergies reported.

Social History:
- Able to drive to GP/clinic; described as a short drive (exact duration not documented).
- Smoking, alcohol, and drug use: not discussed.

Family History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed (telemedicine). No vitals documented.

Investigations:
- None performed during this consult. Plan for pulse oximetry at in-person visit.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute wheeze and shortness of breath—suspected asthma exacerbation versus allergic response to dust exposure.
  - Plan:
    - Attend in-person GP/clinic for assessment, including oxygen saturation (pulse oximetry) and further evaluation to distinguish asthma vs allergic cause.
    - Consider taking an over-the-counter antihistamine en route or obtain one at the clinic; none available at home.
    - Possible need for oral steroids depending on in-person assessment.
    - Letter to GP to be provided via app; in-person consultation expected to be brief.
- General Plan items:
  - No additional safety-netting advice documented.
  - Follow-up with GP after in-person evaluation (timing not specified).

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Full vitals (including O2 saturation), respiratory exam, peak flow/spirometry, detailed medication reconciliation (including inhaler type and use), smoking status, detailed allergy verification (drug vs environmental), asthma control and action plan, red-flag/safety-net advice.
- Internal conflicts: None noted; time to GP described as “maybe minutes’ drive” (unclear duration).
- Transcript quality: Some audio/video interruptions and incomplete phrases; minor inaudible sections.
